newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts lower but trade cautious.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts lower but trade cautious.

text.p: London's October white sugar contract backed off its recent new life-high on Wednesday as a mixed bag of sellers moved to take profits after this week's fund-led buying wave, traders said.
Trade players were cited as leading the selling pack after October burst $5.50 higher on Tuesday to score a new high of $330.20.

The funds were generally thought to have completed their October buying for the time being, although there was still a small amount of buying suporting the position earlier in the day at just under $330.
But the main talk was of the increased fund position in London and how trade players would react to it.
"It caught the trade on the hop," said one dealer.
"They (funds) have pushed it, finished buying and now nobody knows what to do," he said.
The weakness from profit-taking was coupled with the usual round of hedging ahead of Wednesday's weekly European Union tender for sugar export licences.
At 1600 GMT October was down $2.70 at $327.00 and December down $1.70 at $322.10. Volume amounted to 1,475 lots, half of which was in the spot contract.
Traders also cited interest in the nearby October/October arbitrage against the New York market, with the differential narrowing to under $74 from around $76 earlier this week.
October also dominated activity in Paris, usual for a Wednesday on account of the EU tender, down $1.00 at $327.50. December was down 80 cents at $322.20 and Matif volume totalled 638 lots.
